text:
Tim H: FYI we keep hitting saturation in eu-west on the small models when traffic has lots of long-context batches. Thinking we should switch to token-based TPM/RPM limits instead of just requests/sec. Anyone object? :thinking:

Maria K: +1 from me. requests/sec hides the real cost since 1 request can be 10k tokens. Need per-tenant token accounting for admission control.

Jules L: What exact metric do you want to enforce? tokens/min per-tenant? tokens/second for realtime? Also need to map tokens -> GPU capacity units.

Tim H: Proposal: convert each model's measured end-to-end throughput into tokens-per-GPU-minute (TPGM). Admission control uses tenant_token_quota = committed_tpgm * allocation_multiplier. Then enforce both tenant_tokens_per_minute and concurrent_inflight limit.

Anita P: sketch calc I ran this morning: one g5.12x can sustain ~1.2M tokens/min on redwood-compact at 512 context (measured). If we want 10% headroom for autoscaling, usable = 1.08M tpm. For 50 tenants equal share -> ~21.6k tpm each.

Maria K: Nice. We should also include batching efficiency factor. Long sequences get better kernel utilization, short ones worse. Suggest storing per-model efficiency multiplier E in model catalog. Effective_TPGM = measured_TPGM * E.

Tim H: Exactly. Example enforcement math I put in ops doc: 
```
# per-GPU capacity (measured) = 1_200_000 tokens/min
headroom = 0.9
usable = 1_200_000 * headroom  # = 1_080_000
# tenant share if 50 tenants pinned to node
tenant_tokens_per_min = usable / 50 # = 21_600
# translate to TPM (requests) depends on avg_token_per_request
avg_tokens = 320
tenant_TPM = tenant_tokens_per_min / avg_tokens * 60 # convert min -> hour? wait TPM = tokens/min / tokens_per_request so = 21_600 / 320 = 67.5 requests/min = 4050 requests/hour
```
(we left comments but core idea is tokens->requests using avg_token estimate).

Jules L: A couple of operational asks: 1) who provides avg_tokens per tenant (client-level telemetry), 2) how do we handle sudden spikes where avg_tokens changes (streaming long chat)?

Tim H: For 1) source is per-route histograms in console (last 24h). For 2) enforce short-term burst buckets: allow bursts up to 2x for 1 minute, then throttle to sustained token rate. Also fallback route to smaller model if tenant exceeds budget.

Anita P: Queueing behavior question: do we want to queue some tokens or fail fast? Queue depth eats GPU memory (KV caches) and increases tail latency. My vote: fail fast for interactive routes, queue (with timeout) for batch/async routes.

Maria K: Agree. Add route metadata: "latency_slo": "interactive|async" and admission policy picks failfast vs queue. We can application-tag requests so routing knows.

capacity-bot: new-metric token_capacity_used updated for model redwood-compact/eu-west: current=78% threshold=85%

Jules L: Ops change: update admission controller to check tokens_in_flight + tokens_requested <= tenant_token_allowance and tokens_requested <= node_remaining_tokens. If false -> either enqueue (async) or 429 (interactive).

Tim H: Implementation note: in the controller we should store integer token counters to avoid float drift. Keep window = 60s sliding. Also emit metrics: tenant_token_usage, tenant_token_denied, node_token_headroom.

Anita P: Can we add a simple config proto? 
```yaml
admission_policy:
  mode: hybrid # failfast for interactive, queue for async
  per_tenant:
    window_sec: 60
    tokens_allowed: "derived_from_commitment_or_default"
    burst_multiplier: 2
  per_node:
    headroom_pct: 0.1
    measured_tpgm_metric: redwood.metrics.tpgm
```

Maria K: +1. Want to add a short-term experiment: pick 10 midsize tenants in eu-west, enable token-based limits for them next week and compare dropped/queued rates and p99 latency.

Tim H: I'll schedule the experiment. Action items: (1) Jules to PR admission-controller changes, (2) Anita to add config proto + tests, (3) Maria to pick tenants and prepare dashboards, (4) capacity-bot to annotate node headroom during test.

Jules L: I'll start the PR tonight and add unit tests for sliding token window.

Maria K: I'll pick the tenants and add dashboard. Will @sre-team review the test plan?

Anita P: Putting test plan in #eng-infra/ops-runbook after draft.

Tim H: Thanks all. If we see this lowers cost/latency tradeoff, we can roll out more broadly. :rocket:
